title: ACE2 Receptor Expression and SARS-CoV-2 Cell Entry in Human Airway Epithelium
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 uses the ACE2 receptor as its primary entry point into human airway epithelial cells. The spike protein binds ACE2 and is primed by the host protease TMPRSS2, facilitating membrane fusion. High ACE2 expression in nasal epithelium may explain early upper respiratory tract infection.
authors: Chen L; Wang Y; Zhou H

title: Remdesivir Inhibits SARS-CoV-2 Replication in Vitro
abstract: Remdesivir, a nucleotide analogue prodrug, was shown to inhibit SARS-CoV-2 replication in Vero E6 cells by targeting the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The drug had previously been evaluated against Ebola virus and MERS-CoV.
authors: Gao Q; Sun J; Li M

title: Hydroxychloroquine and Azithromycin Combination Therapy for COVID-19: An Open-Label Trial
abstract: An open-label non-randomized trial evaluated hydroxychloroquine, alone and combined with azithromycin, in patients with COVID-19. Viral load reduction was reported, though the study was later criticized for methodological limitations.
authors: Gautret P; Lagier JC; Parola P

title: Clinical Features of Patients Infected with 2019 Novel Coronavirus in Wuhan, China
abstract: This retrospective study describes the clinical characteristics of 41 patients admitted to Jin Yin-tan Hospital, Wuhan, with laboratory-confirmed 2019-nCoV infection. Common symptoms included fever, cough, and myalgia. Some patients developed acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).
authors: Huang C; Wang Y; Li X

title: BNT162b2 mRNA COVID-19 Vaccine Elicits Robust Neutralizing Antibody Response
abstract: The BNT162b2 mRNA vaccine, developed by Pfizer and BioNTech, encodes the SARS-CoV-2 spike glycoprotein. Phase I/II trial participants developed neutralizing antibodies at levels comparable to or exceeding convalescent sera.
authors: Mulligan MJ; Lyke KE; Kitchin N

title: Cytokine Storm and Interleukin-6 in Severe COVID-19 Pneumonia
abstract: Severe COVID-19 cases are associated with a hyperinflammatory state termed cytokine storm, characterized by elevated interleukin-6 (IL-6), IL-1, and TNF-alpha. Tocilizumab, an IL-6 receptor antagonist, was proposed as a treatment for critically ill patients.
authors: Mehta P; McAuley DF; Brown M

title: Angiotensin-Converting Enzyme 2 as a SARS-CoV-2 Receptor: Structural Insights
abstract: Cryo-electron microscopy structures reveal how the SARS-CoV-2 spike receptor-binding domain engages ACE2. These structural insights inform the design of neutralizing antibodies and vaccine immunogens targeting the spike protein.
authors: Yan R; Zhang Y; Li Y

title: Dexamethasone Reduces Mortality in Hospitalized COVID-19 Patients Requiring Oxygen
abstract: The RECOVERY trial found that dexamethasone, a corticosteroid, reduced 28-day mortality among hospitalized COVID-19 patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation or supplemental oxygen, but not among patients without respiratory support.
authors: Horby P; Lim WS; Emberson JR

title: TMPRSS2 Protease Inhibitor Camostat Mesylate Blocks SARS-CoV-2 Cell Entry
abstract: Camostat mesylate, a clinically approved TMPRSS2 inhibitor, partially blocked SARS-CoV-2 entry into lung cells in vitro. Combined blockade of TMPRSS2 and cathepsin B/L pathways fully prevented viral entry.
authors: Hoffmann M; Kleine-Weber H; Schroeder S

title: Convalescent Plasma Therapy for Severe COVID-19: A Case Series
abstract: A case series of critically ill COVID-19 patients treated with convalescent plasma from recovered donors showed clinical improvement and reduced viral load, suggesting passive antibody transfer as a potential treatment strategy.
authors: Shen C; Wang Z; Zhao F

title: Global Spread and Genomic Epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 Variants
abstract: Phylogenetic analysis of SARS-CoV-2 genomes collected from Wuhan, Italy, and the United States traced the global spread of the virus and identified emerging spike protein mutations, including D614G, associated with increased transmissibility.
authors: Korber B; Fischer WM; Gnanakaran S

title: World Health Organization Guidance on COVID-19 Infection Prevention and Control
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) issued interim guidance for infection prevention and control during health care when COVID-19 is suspected, including recommendations on personal protective equipment and isolation precautions.
authors: World Health Organization

title: Moderna mRNA-1273 Vaccine Phase 1 Trial in Older Adults
abstract: The mRNA-1273 vaccine, developed by Moderna and the NIH, was evaluated in adults aged 56 and older. The vaccine encodes a prefusion-stabilized SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and elicited neutralizing antibody titers comparable to younger participants.
authors: Anderson EJ; Rouphael NG; Widge AT

title: Loss of Smell and Taste as Early Symptoms of SARS-CoV-2 Infection
abstract: A multicenter study found that anosmia and dysgeusia were common early symptoms among COVID-19 patients, often preceding other respiratory symptoms, and could serve as useful markers for early case identification.
authors: Lechien JR; Chiesa-Estomba CM; De Siati DR

title: Furin Cleavage Site in the SARS-CoV-2 Spike Protein Enhances Pathogenicity
abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein contains a furin cleavage site absent in closely related coronaviruses. This motif is proteolytically processed by furin and enhances cell-cell fusion and pathogenicity in human airway cells.
authors: Hoffmann M; Kleine-Weber H; Pohlmann S

title: Children and COVID-19: Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome (MIS-C)
abstract: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C) temporally associated with SARS-CoV-2 infection presents with persistent fever, elevated inflammatory markers, and multiorgan involvement, resembling Kawasaki disease in some cases.
authors: Riphagen S; Gomez X; Gonzalez-Martinez C

title: Favipiravir as a Potential Treatment for COVID-19
abstract: Favipiravir, a broad-spectrum antiviral originally developed for influenza, inhibits the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase. Early open-label studies in China suggested favipiravir shortened viral clearance time compared to lopinavir/ritonavir.
authors: Cai Q; Yang M; Liu D

title: Airborne Transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in Indoor Environments
abstract: Evidence from restaurant and choir practice outbreak investigations supports aerosol transmission of SARS-CoV-2 in poorly ventilated indoor spaces, with implications for ventilation guidance and mask policy.
authors: Morawska L; Milton DK

title: Lopinavir-Ritonavir Trial in Hospitalized Adults with COVID-19
abstract: A randomized, controlled, open-label trial of lopinavir-ritonavir, an HIV protease inhibitor combination, in hospitalized adults with severe COVID-19 found no significant benefit over standard care.
authors: Cao B; Wang Y; Wen D

title: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention COVID-19 Response and Surveillance
abstract: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) established nationwide surveillance systems and testing guidance for COVID-19, coordinating with state health departments during the early phase of the pandemic in Wuhan-linked travel cases.
authors: CDC COVID-19 Response Team
